question.text: High portfolio turnover from frequent rebalancing tends to result in:

answer.text: Higher transaction costs, brokerage, bid-ask/liquidity cost, and tax liabilities on realised gains

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats rebalancing as having explicit costs: transaction cost and brokerage on the trades, bid-ask spread as a liquidity/impact cost when unwinding positions, and tax liabilities on the gains realised at sale. Frequent rebalancing increases all of these. The Trap: Frequent rebalancing does not automatically improve after-tax returns; the cost stack often offsets the marginal allocation benefit. Note: Cost discipline is therefore a core part of designing the rebalancing rule in the IPS.
